evidence: Injected five duplicate-callback classes (python3 -I duplicate_callback_injector.py, exit 1) and ran 13 unittest cases (python3 -I -m unittest discover, 13 tests OK). A byte-for-byte replay repeated five times behaved correctly: the first was ingested, the next four were suppressed, and exactly one ingestion file, one registry INGESTION row and one PARENT_INGESTED event existed. Three other duplicate shapes broke the bar. A retry whose timestamps were regenerated kept the transaction identity identical (same idempotency key, lease, fence, attempt, result commit and artifact hashes) but changed the document bytes, so it was not suppressed and produced two ingestion files, two registry rows and two PARENT_INGESTED events for one transaction; the real emit_result.py was confirmed to set readback_verified_at and committed_at from utc_now() on every run, which is exactly this shape. Forcing two ingestions to interleave inside the check-then-write window with one frozen clock produced two registry rows and two PARENT_INGESTED events for one logical ingestion, and with clocks one second apart the second writer raised FileExistsError: immutable file differs on the ingestion file, crashing the coordinator out of ingestion. Two duplicate external effects were observed and zero false completions. metrics/work-unit-runs.jsonl held 0 rows after every class, so ingest_result writes no metric row at all. The repair candidate keys suppression on the transaction identity and claims it by exclusive file creation; three identical replays plus one regenerated retry collapsed to a single ingestion, registry row and event.
falsifiable_hypothesis: A duplicated callback is harmless and cannot double-count a unit or a metric row.
limitations: The concurrency result is produced by a deterministic interleaving of the check-then-write window rather than by wall-clock racing, so the timing probability of hitting it in production is not measured here, only its reachability and its consequence.

The deliverable's metric-row clause cannot be satisfied as written because ingest_result writes no metric row; the append-only work-unit registry is the only per-ingestion durable effect that exists to count.
provider_run_id is NOT_SUPPORTED because this runtime exposes no subagent spawn tool and therefore no separate provider run identifier.
